prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
All 41 test cases pass and the sample log yields the two expected dates; the work is done, so I report the result.

**Goal**
One regex in `./regex.txt` that, over a whole log with `re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)`, returns the last real `YYYY-MM-DD` date on every line containing a valid IPv4 address, and nothing on lines without one.

**What I found / the regex**
```
^(?=.*(?<![\w.])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)(?![\w.])).* (?<![\w-])((?:(?:19|20)\d{2})-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1\d|2[0-9])))(?![\w-])
```
How it works:
- `^(?=.*<ipv4>)` — anchor at line start, lookahead asserts the line contains a valid IPv4 (each part `0-255`, no leading zeros, no letter/digit/dot directly before or after).
- `.* ` — greedy prefix pushes the match to the last date on the line (requires a space before the date, which holds for the log format).
- The date is the single capture group: year `19xx`/`20xx`, month `01-12`, day valid per month (31/30/29), with `(?<![\w-])` / `(?![\w-])` so a letter or digit right before or after disqualifies it.

**Assumptions (brief left open)**
- "February allowed up to the 29th in every year" → `02-29` is accepted in all years (no leap-year check).
- Year range `1900-2099` (covers the log's 2026 and any realistic server date).
- "Letter or digit right before/after" → I also block a `.` or `-` adjacent to a date (e.g. `x.2026-04-09` or `2026-04-09-5` don't count), and a `.` adjacent to an address (e.g. `10.1.1.1.2` doesn't count), since those are the natural "not a standalone token" readings.
- The date is separated from surrounding text by whitespace (as in the sample log); the greedy `.* ` relies on a space before the date.

**How I know it is right**
Ran `python tmp_verify.py`: **41/41 passed**, and the sample `server.log` yields exactly `['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05']` (lines 1 and 3 have addresses + dates; lines 2, 4, 5 give nothing). The 41 cases cover: valid/invalid addresses (leading zero, 256, 300, 255.255.255.255, 0.0.0.0, letter/digit/dot adjacency), last-of-multiple dates, date adjacency (letter/digit before/after), invalid dates (Feb 30, Apr 31, month 13, day 00), and Feb 29 in every year.

No browser tabs, windows, or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
